finalOutput:
The game is complete. `snake_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html` (617 lines, single file — HTML + CSS + JS, no dependencies) was created successfully. Open it in any browser to play.

**What's implemented:**

- **30×30 grid** rendered on a canvas with a neon aesthetic
- **Classic mechanics** — snakes move continuously in 4 directions, grow when eating food, and die on wall collision or hitting any snake body (including their own)
- **Keyboard controls** — Player 1: Arrow keys, Player 2: WASD (with 180°-turn prevention)
- **CPU AI** — pathfinding toward food (greedy direction scoring with wall/body avoidance and lookahead so it doesn't trap itself)
- **Three game modes**, selectable from the start menu:
  1. **Human vs Human** (Arrows vs WASD)
  2. **CPU vs Human**
  3. **CPU vs CPU** (watch two AIs battle)
- **Live score display** — both snakes' scores shown above the board during gameplay
- **Start menu** — mode selection via click or keys 1/2/3
- **Game over screen** — shows the winner and final scores
- **Keypress restart** — press **R** (or Enter) on the game-over screen to replay the same mode, **Esc** returns to the menu

Two snakes compete on the same board simultaneously; food respawns after being eaten, and the last snake alive (or higher score on mutual collision) wins.

{"path":"snake_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW complete single-file HTML file implementing a two-snake Snake game with embedded CSS and JavaScript (no external resources). Requirements:

STRUCTURE
- One HTML file: <style> in <head>, <script> at end of <body>. Dark neon arcade aesthetic (dark background, glowing accents), centered layout, monospace/retro font stack.
- A <canvas> for the game, plus HTML overlay screens for the menu and game-over screens, and a scoreboard bar above the canvas.

GAME CONSTANTS
- Grid: 30x30 cells. Canvas 600x600 px (cell size 20px). Draw a subtle grid.

CORE GAMEPLAY
- Two snakes play simultaneously on the same grid. Snake 1 starts near left side moving right; Snake 2 starts near right side moving left. Each starts with length 3.
- Fixed timestep game loop (~110 ms per tick, may slightly speed up as food is eaten). Snakes move continuously one cell per tick in their current direction; direction changes via input queue so 180-degree reversals are ignored.
- Food: keep 3 food items on the board at all times; spawn at random empty cells (never on any snake or other food). Eating food grows that snake by 1 and increments its score by 1.
- Death conditions for a snake: hitting a wall, hitting its own body, hitting the other snake's body. Head-on head collision (both heads enter the same cell) kills both. When a snake dies the game ends immediately; the surviving snake wins (draw if both die simultaneously).
- Scores (food eaten per snake) displayed live during gameplay in the scoreboard, labeled e.g. "P1: 0" / "P2: 0" or "CPU 1" / "CPU 2" depending on mode, each in its snake's color.

CONTROLS
- Player 1: Arrow keys. Player 2: W/A/S/D.
- On game over screen: pressing Enter, Space, or R restarts the same mode instantly; pressing Escape or M returns to the start menu. On the menu: keys 1/2/3 select a mode (in addition to clickable buttons).

CPU AI
- Each CPU-controlled snake computes its move every tick: BFS shortest path from its head to the nearest food, treating walls, both snakes' bodies (except tails that will move) as obstacles. Follow the first step of that path.
- If no path to any food exists, fall back to survival: choose any non-lethal move, preferring the move that keeps the most free space (flood-fill count) or follows its own tail.
- CPU must also avoid moving into the cell the other snake's head will likely occupy when possible.

GAME MODES (start menu with three buttons + keys 1/2/3)
1. Human vs Human — P1 arrows, P2 WASD.
2. CPU vs Human — Snake 1 is human (arrows), Snake 2 is CPU.
3. CPU vs CPU — both snakes AI; runs automatically as a demo battle.

SCREENS / STATE MACHINE
- States: MENU, PLAYING, GAMEOVER. Menu shows title, the three mode buttons, and a controls legend. Game over screen shows winner text (e.g. "Player 1 Wins!", "CPU 2 Wins!", "Draw!"), final scores, and restart/menu hints. Show a brief 3-2-1 or "Get Ready" countdown optional (keep simple: short pause before snakes start moving is fine).

RENDERING
- Draw each snake in a distinct color (e.g. green and cyan/orange) with a brighter head and eyes indicating direction; food as glowing red dots. Clear and redraw the whole canvas each tick.
- Clean, well-commented, self-contained vanilla JavaScript. No libraries, no external assets. Ensure the code is complete and runnable by just opening the file in a browser."}
